links.outcome: Association of GenAI use with self-reported behaviors indicative of knowledge collapse or deskilling
links.effect: GenAI use was independently associated with favorable behaviors: thorough examination (aOR 1.42, 95% CI 1.18-1.70) and appropriate antimicrobial use (aOR 1.57, 95% CI 1.32-1.87). Only 13% (144/1110) of users relied on GenAI as primary reference for differential diagnoses.
links.quote: Although GenAI use was not associated with self-reported behaviors indicative of knowledge collapse at this stage, GenAI literacy among resident physicians in Japan remains limited, particularly among nonusers.

links.outcome: Resident physicians' GenAI literacy, including understanding of confabulation and ethical considerations
links.effect: Understanding of confabulation: 74.1% of users vs 58.4% of nonusers. Fairness examined by 47.3% and transparency by 49.8% overall; awareness lower among nonusers (41.5% and 43.8%).
links.quote: Although GenAI use was not associated with self-reported behaviors indicative of knowledge collapse at this stage, GenAI literacy among resident physicians in Japan remains limited, particularly among nonusers.

screen.reason: This is a nationwide cross-sectional survey evaluating the real-world use of generative AI as a search engine among resident physicians in Japan, examining AI literacy and clinical behaviors.
